name: Official UK confirmation of remote IT-worker typology detection

attribution.legal_posture: Official country-level detection statement covering a national pattern; named case, victim, person, enforcement result, and scale remain unreported.

caveats: Source-described presentation as a third-country national is a deception pattern; nationality profiling and legitimate-applicant rejection require source-backed evidence.
The officials supplied testimony lacking worker, employer, victim, count, payment route, and enforcement outcome; prevalence and company attribution remain unassessed.

statements: Use this source-qualified context for governance or corroborated behavior-based review, never as standalone identity or nationality attribution.
limitations: No single nationality, geography, language, education history, technical skill, remote-work preference, interview anomaly, authentication event, or device signal establishes fraud or DPRK attribution.

statements: In official parliamentary evidence, UK sanctions officials stated that authorities had detected the remote IT-worker revenue typology in the United Kingdom and described the advisory as arising through international DPRK-sanctions coordination.
limitations: The officials provided no worker, employer, victim, count, payment route, or enforcement outcome, so the testimony cannot support prevalence estimates or company-level attribution.
Source-described presentation as a third-country national is a deception pattern, not a basis for nationality profiling or rejecting legitimate foreign applicants.
infrastructure.method_and_source_boundary: authoritative first-party testimony from HM Treasury and OFSI officials; intentionally non-granular to protect intelligence and compliance activity

sources.support: Supports the official UK statement that the typology had been detected and discussed through sanctions coordination.
